mainTopic: Fixing a מבוי, keeping a שיתוף מבואות valid, and how much and what food an ערוב needs
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. The גמרא explains why a source lets residents be forced to fix their מבוי: either that alley had no walls, or a physical fix differs from a side arrangement like an ערוב. Next, רב חייא בר אשי and ריש לקיש argue over whether a לחי or a קורה may be made from אשירה wood. The rule of כתותי מכתת שיעוריה explains why a קורה is harder. A new משנה then teaches how to keep a שיתוף מבואות valid: shrunken food may be topped up quietly, but new residents must be told. It also sets the amount of food (two meals for many residents, a גרוגרת each for few), and רבי יוסי limits that amount to when the ערוב is first made. The גמרא asks what kind of added food the משנה means and resolves it with two answers. It then learns from the משנה that the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה about including people without their knowledge. Finally, it defines 'many' as eighteen or more people, since two meals equal eighteen figs. A new משנה begins with רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע arguing over which foods may be used for an ערוב.

steps.title: That case is different because there are no walls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the source allowing residents to be forced is a special case: the מבוי there has no proper walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because there are no partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a difficulty from an earlier source, which says residents can be forced to fix their מבוי. It explains that the source is talking about a special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that source the מבוי has no proper מחיצות, so it is broken open and unprotected. That is why the residents can be forced to set up something that closes it off. Where the מבוי already has walls, nobody can be forced to join a שיתוף מבואות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (a way of setting a source apart)
An alleyway that opens onto the street
Joining the food of an alleyway's residents so they may carry on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers a question that came on the previous amud. The phrase "שאני התם" always means the גמרא is setting a source apart from our case, not stating a brand-new rule.

phrases.english: It is different there
because there are no partitions.
phrases.notes: The alley is broken open, so the residents can be forced to close it off, at least for safety.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a challenge raised on the previous amud, from a source that allows forcing residents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא of the facts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seemed to show that residents can always be forced to join in fixing their מבוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forcing is allowed only where the מבוי lacks walls. Where it has walls, no one is forced to join a שיתוף.

steps.title: Another version: something done 'from the side' is different
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the answer says that making an ערוב is a side matter, not a change to the alley itself, so no one can be forced into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: from the side it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way of reporting the same answer. This version focuses on what kind of action is being demanded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לחי or קורה is a physical fix to the alley itself, so residents can be forced to make one. Preparing an ערוב or שיתוף is not a change to the alley. It is a side arrangement, so no one can be forced to take part.

keyTerms.meaning: From the side, a side matter
A halachic arrangement that permits carrying on שבת

phrases.english: Another version:
from the side it is different.
phrases.notes: An ערוב is a side matter and does not change the alley itself (מאיר נתיב).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different reported version of the answer given in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by the type of action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every action that helps the alley can be forced on its residents.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a physical fix to the alley can be forced. A side arrangement like an ערוב cannot.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that residents cannot always be forced to join a שיתוף. They differ only in why the source about forcing is different: no walls, or a physical fix versus a side matter.

steps.title: Dispute: may a לחי or a קורה be made from an אשירה?
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי says you may make a לחי from אשירה wood. ריש לקיש says you may even make a קורה from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב חייא בר אשי said: One may make a לחי from an אשירה. And רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: One may make a קורה from an אשירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a dispute between two אמוראים about using wood from an אשירה to fix a מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not get any benefit from an אשירה, and it must be burned. Even so, both אמוראים allow using it for a מצוה like fixing the מבוי, because מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו (doing a מצוה does not count as benefit). They disagree only about how far this goes: just a לחי, or also a קורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
A side post at the entrance of a מבוי
A cross beam over the entrance of a מבוי
A tree worshipped as עבודה זרה; benefit from it is forbidden
Doing a מצוה is not counted as getting benefit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think they argue about whether benefit from an אשירה is allowed. Both agree it is forbidden. The question is only whether using it for a מצוה counts, and whether the wood still has the required size.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said:
One may make a side post from an asheira.
And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
One may make a cross beam from an asheira.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר, רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר: עוֹשִׂין לֶחִי אֲשֵׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the materials used to fix a מבוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חייא בר אשי allows a לחי from an אשירה. ריש לקיש allows a קורה from an אשירה.

steps.title: How the two opinions relate: wood that must be burned has no size
steps.stepSummary: Whoever allows a קורה surely allows a לחי. Whoever allows only a לחי forbids a קורה, because wood that must be burned is treated as already crushed and lacks the required size.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said a cross beam would all the more so allow a side post. But the one who said a side post would not allow a cross beam, because its size is considered crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how far each opinion goes and gives the reason רב חייא בר אשי does not allow a קורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשירה must be burned, so halacha treats it as if it were already crushed to dust (כתותי מכתת שיעוריה). A קורה must be at least a טפח wide, so wood treated as having no size cannot work. A לחי has no minimum width, so it still works. ריש לקיש allows even a קורה, so he clearly does not apply this concern here, and his ruling includes a לחי all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said (refers back to an opinion)
Its size is considered crushed: something that must be burned is treated as already having no size
A handbreadth, the minimum width of a קורה

steps.whatToRemember: A קורה needs a minimum size and a לחי does not. So, according to רב חייא בר אשי, the rule of כתותי מכתת שיעוריה disqualifies an אשירה only for a קורה. ריש לקיש allows both.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of כתותי מכתת שיעוריה shows up all over ש״ס, for example with a לולב of אשירה. It applies only where the halacha requires a minimum size.

phrases.english: The one who said a cross beam may be made from it —
all the more so a side post,
and the one who said a side post —
but a cross beam, no.
Its size is considered crushed.
phrases.notes: An אשירה must be burned, so it counts as having no size. A קורה needs a טפח; a לחי needs no minimum width.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹרָה — כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן לֶחִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far each opinion in step 3 reaches and why they differ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשירה may be used for a לחי according to everyone. According to רב חייא בר אשי it may not be used for a קורה, because כתותי מכתת שיעוריה.

steps.title: Topping up the food and adding new residents
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on two problems with an existing שיתוף. If the food shrank, one may add food without telling anyone. If new residents joined, one may add them but must tell them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the food got smaller, he adds more and gives the others a share in it, and he does not need to tell them. If new people joined them, he adds food and gives them a share, and he does need to tell them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It explains how to keep the alley's shared food (the שיתוף) valid when something changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two cases. When the food shrinks, the people are already part of the שיתוף, so topping it up simply keeps their existing arrangement working, and no announcement is needed. When new residents arrive, they are being brought into the arrangement for the first time, so the משנה requires that they be told.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the base text being learned)
Gives a legal share (ownership) to others

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases look almost the same, since both say מוסיף ומזכה. The only difference is the last phrase: shrinking food means 'no need to tell,' while new people means 'must tell.'

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If the food diminished,
he adds and confers possession [to the others],
phrases.notes: He adds some of his own food and gives everyone a share in it.

phrases.english: and he need not inform [them].
If [new residents] were added to them,
he adds and confers possession [to them],
and he must inform [them].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה. It moves from the material used for a לחי or קורה to the practical upkeep of the שיתוף food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that shrank may be topped up without informing anyone. New residents may be added, but they must be informed.

steps.title: How much food is needed?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the required amount of food is for the שיתוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much is the required amount?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up its next rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 talked about the food becoming 'too little.' That raises the obvious question of what counts as enough. This question opens that discussion.

phrases.english: How much is their measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 5 assumed there is a minimum amount of food. This step asks what that minimum is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of food needed for a valid שיתוף מבואות.

steps.title: Two meals for many people, a dried fig each for few
steps.stepSummary: If the residents are many, food for two meals covers everyone. If they are few, each person needs a גרוגרת-sized amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there are many people, food for two meals is enough for all of them. When there are few people, a dried-fig amount for each one is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question. It gives two different amounts, depending on how many residents there are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two meals is a fixed amount for the whole group. With a large group, a fig-size portion per person would add up to more than two meals, so the משנה caps the requirement at two meals. With a small group, a fig-size portion per person is the smaller amount, so that is enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Two meals is the total for the whole group, not two meals per person.

phrases.english: When they are many,
food for two meals for all of them.
When they are few,
like a dried fig for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For many residents, food for two meals for the whole group. For few residents, a גרוגרת-sized amount per person.

steps.title: The amount applies only when first setting up the ערוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the required amount matters only when the ערוב is first made. Leftovers of an existing ערוב stay valid at any size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: When does this rule apply? At the start of the ערוב. But for the leftovers of a ערוב, any amount is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי narrows the rule from step 7. It applies only when the ערוב is first set up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full amount is needed only to create the ערוב in the first place. Once it was made properly, it stays valid even if it later shrinks, as long as some of it remains. רבי יוסי is adding a limit to the amounts just given in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who adds a limit to the rule
When does this apply? (a formula that limits a rule)
The start of the ערוב, when it is first made
Leftovers of a ערוב already made

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key difference between starting a ערוב and keeping one going. A ערוב needs the full amount to be made, but much less to stay valid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In what case are these words said?
At the beginning of an eiruv,
but with the remnants of an eiruv,
any amount [is enough].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the amounts given in step 7 to the moment the ערוב is first made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full amount is needed only to set up a ערוב. Leftovers of an existing ערוב are valid at any size.

steps.title: Courtyards still make a ערוב so children won't forget
steps.stepSummary: Even when the alley has a שיתוף, the courtyards still make their own ערוב. This is only so that children do not forget the practice of ערוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only said to make a ערוב in the courtyards so that the children would not forget [the practice of ערוב].
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by explaining why courtyards make their own ערוב even though the alley's שיתוף already exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself, the alley's שיתוף could have been enough. Still, the courtyards are told to make a ערוב as well, so that the practice stays visible. Otherwise, children growing up would never see a courtyard ערוב and would not know it exists.
steps.whatToRemember: Summary of the משנה: (1) If the food shrinks, top it up without telling anyone. (2) If new residents join, add them and tell them. (3) The amount is two meals for many people, or a גרוגרת each for few. (4) רבי יוסי: the amount matters only at the start, and leftovers are valid at any size. (5) Courtyards still make their own ערוב, so that children do not forget.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason given is educational, to keep the practice known. It is not that the alley's שיתוף fails to work.

phrases.english: And they only said to make an eiruv in the courtyards
so as not to cause to forget
the children [the practice of eiruv].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אָמְרוּ לְעָרֵב בַּחֲצֵירוֹת אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְשַׁכֵּחַ אֶת הַתִּינוֹקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rules for the alley's שיתוף, the משנה explains why a separate courtyard ערוב is still made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Courtyards make their own ערוב even when a שיתוף exists, so that children do not forget the practice of ערוב.

steps.title: What case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what exact case the משנה's rule about adding food is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking what situation the rule about adding to a shrunken שיתוף refers to. This is a setup line. The next steps test two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one may add food 'without informing' the others. The גמרא wants to know what kind of added food the משנה means. Each possible answer seems to cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing? A standard opening asking for the exact situation
The discussion that analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
With what case are we dealing?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's rule: if the food shrank, one may add without informing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first rule of the משנה (Step 5) to define its case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the added food in the משנה's case match the original kind of food, or is it a different kind?

steps.title: If the added food is the same kind, why mention only 'shrank'?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is adding the same kind of food, the משנה should have said that even a fully used-up שיתוף needs no informing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is about one kind of food, why specifically 'it shrank'? Even if it was completely used up, the same should be true!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer: the person added the same kind of food. It then shows a problem with that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the same kind of food is something the residents already agreed to, so no informing should be needed at all. That would hold even if the food ran out completely. So the משנה's narrow wording 'shrank' seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a possible explanation that will be tested
One kind. The added food is the same kind as the original
Why specifically this case? Asks why the text chose narrow wording

phrases.english: If you say it is about one kind of food,
why specify 'it shrank'?
Even if it was completely used up, it should also be so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּמִין אֶחָד, מַאי אִירְיָא נִתְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the food is the same kind, the law does not depend on whether some food remains. The limited wording is therefore unnecessary.

steps.title: If the added food is a different kind, informing should be needed
steps.stepSummary: If the case is adding a different kind of food, then even when the food only shrank, one should not be allowed to add without informing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about two kinds of food. But then even if it only shrank, one should also not be allowed to add without informing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second possible answer: the person added a different kind of food. It then shows that this answer also seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The residents might not agree to a new kind of food in their שיתוף, so they should be told. If so, the משנה's ruling that no informing is needed seems wrong for this case. The next step brings a source to support this objection.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Moves to the other option
Two kinds. The added food is different from the original

phrases.english: Rather, it is about two kinds of food,
then even if it only shrank, it should also not be allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁנֵי מִינִין, אֲפִילּוּ נִתְמַעֵט נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option fails, the גמרא tries the second option and finds a problem with it too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one may add without informing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different kind of food needs the residents' agreement. So adding it without telling them should not be allowed, even when the food only shrank.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a different kind of food requires informing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when the food is used up, same-kind food needs no informing, but a different kind does.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: If the food was used up, then for the same kind there is no need to inform; for two kinds, one must inform.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the objection in the previous step. The ברייתא teaches that adding a different kind of food requires informing the residents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling covers both earlier options. Same kind needs no informing, which supports the problem in Step 11. Different kind requires informing, which supports the problem in Step 12. At this point, the גמרא assumes the same rule applies even when the food only shrank.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
If the food was used up,
if he adds from the same kind, he need not inform;
if from two kinds, he must inform!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives source backing to the objections in Steps 11 and 12.
steps.raayaObject: Adding a different kind of food requires informing, while the same kind does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a שיתוף whose food was used up.

steps.title: First answer: same kind, and 'shrank' means fully crumbled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers two possible answers. In the first, the case is the same kind of food, and 'נתמעט' really means it crumbled away completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say it is about one kind, and if you wish, say it is about two kinds. If you wish, say one kind: what does 'it shrank' mean? It crumbled away completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says both options can work and gives a separate answer for each. The first answer defends the 'same kind' option by reading the משנה's word differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11's problem was that 'shrank' seemed too narrow. The answer is that נתמעט here means נתמטמט, crumbled away to nothing. So the משנה does cover the case where nothing is left, and the problem is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say. Introduces one of several possible answers
Crumbled away completely, so nothing remained

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read נתמעט here as 'a bit is missing.' In this answer, the גמרא reads it as the food being entirely gone (crumbled away).

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is about one kind,
and if you wish, say it is about two kinds.
If you wish, say it is about one kind,
and what does 'it shrank' mean? It crumbled away completely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִמִּין אֶחָד, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in Step 11 by reinterpreting the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נתמעט means only partly reduced, so the משנה's wording seemed too narrow.
steps.terutzMaskana: נתמעט means completely crumbled away. With the same kind of food, no informing is needed even when nothing is left.

steps.title: Second answer: different kind, but fully used up is a different case
steps.stepSummary: In the second answer, the case is a different kind of food. The ברייתא requires informing only when the food is completely gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you wish, say it is about two kinds: when the food is completely used up, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now defends the 'different kind' option. It does this by limiting the ברייתא to a case where the food is fully gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed the ברייתא's rule also applies when the food only shrank. The answer separates the two cases. When some food remains, the existing שיתוף still stands, so adding even a different kind needs no informing. When it is fully gone, adding is like starting over, so the residents must be told.

keyTerms.meaning: Is different. Separates one case from another

steps.whatToRemember: The two answers: (1) same kind of food, and 'shrank' means fully crumbled, so no informing is ever needed for the same kind; (2) different kind of food, and informing is needed only when nothing is left. As long as some food remains, one may add without telling anyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second answer teaches that a remaining bit of the original שיתוף keeps it alive. This matches רבי יוסי's idea in Step 8 that leftovers of an existing ערוב stay valid.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is about two kinds,
and when the food is completely used up, it is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִין, כָּלָה שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of the two answers announced in Step 14, this time answering the problem in Steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (the ברייתא is limited to food that is completely used up)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's requirement to inform for a different kind applies even when the food only shrank.
steps.terutzMaskana: The requirement to inform applies only when the food is completely used up. If some remains, even a different kind may be added without informing.

steps.title: The משנה's rule shows the Rabbis disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי quotes רב חסדא: the משנה's requirement to inform new residents shows that the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if new residents were added, he adds food for them, gives them a share, and must tell them. רב שיזבי said in the name of רב חסדא: this shows that רבי יהודה's colleagues disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רב חסדא then draws a conclusion from it about a מחלוקת with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires telling the new residents before including them. That means you cannot include someone in this kind of עירוב without his knowledge. רב חסדא says this goes against רבי יהודה, who allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: He adds food and gives them a share in it
This shows / we can learn from this

phrases.english: If others were added to them, he adds and confers possession, etc.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. The full line ends with the requirement to inform them.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said that Rav Ḥisda said:
This is to say (we learn from this)

phrases.aramaic: חֲלוּקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: that his colleagues disagree with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of a shrunken or used-up שיתוף to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's requirement to inform new residents shows that the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own statement about an עירוב made without the person's knowledge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה where רבי יהודה says the 'knowledge' rule applies only to עירובי תחומין, not to עירובי חצירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יהודה said, when does this rule apply? Only to עירובי תחומין. But for עירובי חצירות, one may make an עירוב for someone with his knowledge or without it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for רבי יהודה's view, which רב חסדא said the משנה disagrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב for שבת boundaries can hurt a person, because walking farther in one direction means less distance the other way. That is why he must know about it. An עירוב חצירות only helps him, so רבי יהודה allows making it without asking him.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
In what case is this said? (limiting a rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why someone might think informing is not needed. Something that only benefits a person can usually be done for him without his knowledge.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case is this said —
regarding joining of boundaries;
but regarding joining of courtyards —

phrases.aramaic: מְעָרְבִין בֵּין לְדַעַת וּבֵין שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת.
phrases.english: one may make an eruv either with his knowledge or without his knowledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion רב חסדא said the משנה argues with.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה allows an עירוב חצירות without the person's knowledge.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה quoting רבי יהודה (עירובין ז:יא).

steps.title: Isn't the disagreement obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חסדא had to say this. Clearly the משנה, which requires informing, disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: his conclusion seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion says you must inform, and רבי יהודה says you need not. That looks like a plain מחלוקת, so what new thing is רב חסדא teaching?

phrases.english: It is obvious that they disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב חסדא's statement teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two rulings plainly contradict each other, so there is no need to point it out.

steps.title: We might have limited the משנה to a courtyard between two alleys
steps.stepSummary: Without רב חסדא, we might think the משנה requires informing only for a courtyard between two alleys. He teaches that it applies to every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this rule applies only to a courtyard between two alleys. But for a courtyard of one alley, say no, you do not need to tell them. So רב חסדא teaches us that the משנה requires informing even there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רב חסדא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A courtyard between two alleys can choose which alley to join, so joining it to one might go against its wishes. That would explain why informing is needed without any argument with רבי יהודה. רב חסדא teaches that the משנה requires informing even for a courtyard on only one alley, where the שיתוף only helps. So there really is a מחלוקת with רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not saying the משנה only deals with a courtyard between two alleys. He is saying the opposite: the משנה requires informing even for a courtyard on one alley.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, new residents must be told even when the שיתוף only benefits them. רבי יהודה disagrees.

phrases.english: Lest you say:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּחָצֵר שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי מְבוֹאוֹת,
phrases.english: this applies only to a courtyard between two alleyways,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חָצֵר שֶׁל מָבוֹי אֶחָד, אֵימָא לָא.
phrases.english: but a courtyard of one alleyway, say no (no need to inform).
He teaches us (that one must inform even there).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a reasonable mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires informing only for a courtyard that could choose between two alleys, so it might not argue with רבי יהודה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה requires informing in every case, even for a courtyard on one alley. So it truly argues with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: How many residents count as 'many'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the amount of food needed and asks how many people count as 'many'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: what is the amount of food needed? (It gives one amount when there are many residents and another when there are few.) The גמרא asks: how many count as 'many'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with the next line of the משנה. It asks a clarifying question about the number of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a fixed amount of food when the residents are many and a smaller amount per person when they are few. To use this rule, we need to know where 'many' begins.

phrases.english: What is its measure, etc.
How many are 'many'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the size of the שיתוף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of residents that counts as 'many' in the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל: eighteen people
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: eighteen people count as 'many'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: eighteen people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a number from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה (step 7) gives two meals as the measure for the many and a גרוגרת each for the few. Eighteen people is the point where the fixed amount of two meals takes over.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Eighteen people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how many count as 'many'.

steps.title: Only exactly eighteen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: does 'many' mean exactly eighteen and no more?
steps.simpleTranslation: Eighteen, and no more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of שמואל's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'eighteen people' sounds like exactly eighteen. But a bigger group is surely also 'many', so the wording seems wrong.

phrases.english: Eighteen, and no more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exact wording of שמואל's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, it would mean nineteen or more are not 'many', which makes no sense.

steps.title: Read it as eighteen and up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: read שמואל as saying eighteen or more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: from eighteen and up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of שמואל's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave the starting point, not an exact number. Any group of eighteen or more counts as 'many'.
steps.whatToRemember: Eighteen or more residents count as 'many' for the size of the שיתוף.

phrases.english: Say: from eighteen and upward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading שמואל's words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eighteen is the minimum. Any larger group also counts as 'many'.

steps.title: Why exactly the number eighteen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל picked the number eighteen as the line for 'many'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about the number eighteen that he chose?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know 'many' means eighteen or more, the גמרא asks why שמואל picked eighteen and not some other number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 22-23 settled that 'many' means eighteen or more. That still does not explain where the number comes from. The גמרא wants the reason behind it, which sets up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He chose / he used (a word or number)

phrases.english: And what is the reason for 'eighteen' that he chose?
phrases.notes: 'He' refers to שמואל, quoted by רב יהודה in Step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the fix in Step 23 and asks for the reason behind the number.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the logic behind using eighteen as the line between 'few' and 'many'?

steps.title: רב יהודה's explanation: when each person gets less than a fig
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק reports his father's rule: if two meals split among the group gives each person less than a fig, they are 'many', and two meals are enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק, son of רב יהודה, said: My father explained it to me personally. Imagine dividing the food of two meals among all the people. If each person would get less than a dried fig, the group counts as 'many', and two meals are enough for all of them. If not, they count as 'few', and each person needs a full fig.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק answers by reporting what his father, רב יהודה, personally explained to him. 'Many' means so many people that two meals, split among them, gives each person less than one fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two meals equal eighteen figs. With more than eighteen people, splitting eighteen figs gives each person less than a fig, so two meals are enough. With fewer than eighteen, a fig per person is the smaller amount, so each person gives a full fig. At exactly eighteen the two measures are the same, which is why eighteen is the turning point.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
A dried fig (a standard size measure)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'many' people need MORE food. The opposite is true: once the group is 'many', a fixed amount (two meals) is enough, even though that gives each person less than a fig.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:
It was explained to me personally by my father:
phrases.notes: His father is רב יהודה, who quoted שמואל in Step 21.

phrases.english: Any case where, if one were to divide
the food of two meals among them

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַגַּעַת גְּרוֹגֶרֶת לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד —
phrases.english: and it would not reach a dried fig for each and every one —
these are the ones called 'many',
and food for two meals is enough.
And if not — these are the ones called 'few'.
phrases.notes: For 'few', each person needs a full fig's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִנֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Many' is defined by math. If two meals divided among the group gives each person less than a fig, they are many, and two meals are enough. Otherwise they are few, and each person needs a fig.

steps.title: A side lesson: two meals equal eighteen figs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this teaching also shows, on the side, that two meals equal eighteen dried figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And along the way, this teaches us that two meals equal eighteen dried figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an extra lesson hidden in רב יהודה's explanation: the size of two meals is eighteen figs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation only works if two meals equal exactly eighteen figs. That is what makes eighteen people the turning point. So without saying it outright, רב יהודה has also told us how much two meals are.
steps.whatToRemember: Two meals = eighteen גרוגרות. If splitting these among the people gives each less than a fig, they are 'many', and two meals are enough. Otherwise each person needs a fig.
steps.whyThisMatters: The measure of two meals as eighteen dried figs is used in other places in halacha that depend on the size of two meals.

phrases.english: And along the way, he teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דִּשְׁתֵּי סְעוּדוֹת הָוְיָין שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה גְּרוֹגְרוֹת.
phrases.english: that two meals equal eighteen dried figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side lesson from the explanation in Step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two meals equal eighteen dried figs, and this is why eighteen people is the line for 'many'.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: any food works except water and salt
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי אליעזר says an עירוב or שיתוף may be made from any food except water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may make an עירוב for courtyards, or a שיתוף for an alley, with any food except water and salt. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It asks what kinds of food may be used for an עירוב, and רבי אליעזר gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the key is that the item is a food. Water and salt are left out because they are not counted as real food. Everything else is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: We join courtyards with an עירוב
We merge an alley with a שיתוף

phrases.english: Mishnah: With anything one may make an eiruv and a shituf,
phrases.notes: עירוב joins courtyards. שיתוף joins an alley.

phrases.english: except for water and salt,
phrases.notes: They are not counted as food.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not tied to the discussion of eighteen figs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any food may be used for an עירוב or שיתוף, except water and salt (רבי אליעזר).

steps.title: רבי יהושע: only a whole loaf works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says an עירוב must be a whole loaf. Even a huge amount in pieces does not work, but even a tiny whole loaf does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: A loaf is an עירוב. Even if the baked bread is as big as a סאה, if it is in pieces, one may not use it for an עירוב. But a loaf as small as an איסר coin, if it is whole, one may use it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע argues with רבי אליעזר. He says what counts for an עירוב is a whole loaf of bread, not the amount of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the deciding factor is whether the loaf is whole, not how big it is. A very large amount in pieces does not work, while a small whole loaf does. This is a different idea from רבי אליעזר, who allows any food.

keyTerms.meaning: A baked amount the size of a סאה (a large measure)
A small coin (here: a very small size)

steps.confusionAlert: For רבי יהושע, size does not decide. A huge amount in pieces is not valid, but a tiny whole loaf is.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כִּכָּר הוּא עֵירוּב,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: A loaf is an eiruv,
even a baked amount of a se'a, if it is in pieces —
one may not make an eiruv with it.
A loaf the size of an issar, if it is whole —
one may make an eiruv with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: כִּכָּר הוּא עֵירוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב for courtyards must be a whole loaf. Pieces do not work, no matter the amount, while a whole loaf of any size does (רבי יהושע).
